title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a smooth projective curve over a finite field F_q with generic point y. E_y is an l-adic representation of the Galois group of the function field. i: y -> X, and i_*(E_y) is the 'middle' or 'intermediate' extension; at each closed point x its stalk is the inertia invariants E_x = E_y^{I_x}. The starred objects are attached to i_*E_y: L^*_{E_y}(t) = L(X, i_*E_y, t) and chi^*(E_y) = chi(X-bar, i_*E_y).

(1) Normalisation and functional equation. Put zeta^*_{E_y}(t) = t^{chi^*/2} L^*_{E_y}(t). The boxed formula reads zeta'^*_{E_y}(1/(qt)) = epsilon'^*(E_y) zeta^*_{E_y}(t). Here the prime on zeta refers to the dual representation E_y^vee, or contragredient. The constant is epsilon'^* = delta^*(E_y) q^{-chi^*/2} (-1)^{chi^*}, where delta^* is essentially det(-F | H^*)-type data.

Check. Poincaré duality on the proper curve gives H^i(X-bar, i_*E) dual to H^{2-i}(X-bar, i_*E^vee)(1). For a polynomial prod(1 - a_i t) of degree n one has prod(1 - a_i t) = (-t)^n (prod a_i) prod(1 - a_i^{-1} t^{-1}). Together these give L(E,t) = eps t^{-chi} L(E^vee, 1/(qt)). Substituting into zeta = t^{chi/2} L gives zeta_{E^vee}(1/(qt)) = q^{-chi/2} eps^{-1} zeta_E(t). So the shape delta * q^{-chi/2} * (sign)^{chi} is right; the signs come from the (-t)^n factors. The line 'q = p^{...}' just records that q is a power of p.

(2) Remark that L^* is not multiplicative ('additif') in E. Take 0 -> E'_y -> E_y -> E''_y -> 0. Since i_* is left exact, there is an exact sequence 0 -> i_*E' -> i_*E -> i_*E'' -> Q -> 0. A first description, Q = Ker(R^1 i_*E' -> R^1 i_*E), was crossed out; it is in fact also correct. Q is a skyscraper sheaf, the sum of j_x(Q_x) over the finitely many points of 'non-simplicité' (ramification) of E''. Its stalks are Q_x = Coker(E_x -> E''_x) = Coker(E^{I_x} -> E''^{I_x}), which lies inside H^1(I_x, E').

Multiplicativity of L-functions in exact sequences of constructible sheaves then gives L^*_E = L^*_{E'} L^*_{E''} L_Q^{-1} = L^*_{E'} L^*_{E''} prod_x P_{Q_x}(t). Here P_{Q_x}(t) = det(1 - F_x t^{deg x} | Q_x) is the local Euler factor of the defect.

(3) Final note: H^2(X-bar, i_*E) is dual to H^0(X-bar, i_*E^vee)(-1). This is Poincaré duality in top degree, used to identify the H^2 factor (the 'denominator') of L^*.

Purpose: preparing the functional equation and epsilon factors for L-functions of Galois representations on curves via middle extensions, in the spirit of Grothendieck's 1964 Bourbaki talk and the later Deligne 'constantes' theory. The page also checks how the global constants behave in exact sequences, which feeds into the non-additivity of epsilon^*.

The neighbouring pages are unrelated Bourbaki drafts (Commutative Algebra ch. VII exercises), filed in the same folder.
errors: No mathematical error. The crossed-out description Q = Ker(R^1 i_*E' -> R^1 i_*E) is actually correct; it was replaced by the more explicit stalk description, not because it was wrong.
The exponent in 'q = p^{...}' is illegible. The machine reading 'p^{1+s}' is doubtful; it is presumably just the statement that q is a power of p.

ideas.what: Normalized zeta^* = t^{chi/2} L^* and its functional equation zeta_{E^vee}(1/(qt)) = eps' zeta_E(t) for the middle extension of a Galois representation on a curve over F_q
ideas.modern_name: Functional equation of L-functions of l-adic sheaves on curves (Poincaré duality + Grothendieck trace formula); global epsilon constant
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Séminaire Bourbaki 279, 1964; SGA5); constants studied by Deligne (1973), Laumon (1987)
ideas.where_published: Formule de Lefschetz et rationalité des fonctions L, Sém. Bourbaki 279 (1964); SGA 5

ideas.what: Defect of multiplicativity of middle-extension L-functions in short exact sequences, given by local factors of Q_x = Coker(E^{I_x} -> E''^{I_x})
ideas.modern_name: Non-exactness of j_* (middle extension); local Euler factor corrections
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA 5 discussions of L-functions of j_*F

ideas.what: Top-degree Poincaré duality H^2(X-bar, i_*E) dual to H^0(X-bar, i_*E^vee)(-1)

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard working computations toward the functional equation of geometric L-functions and its constants. All of it is well known (Grothendieck 1964, Deligne 1973). The only mild curiosity is the explicit bookkeeping of the non-additivity of L^* via ramification defect factors, which is routine.
transcription_corrections: 'i^*_y(E''_y)' should read 'i_*(E''_y)' (the direct image, like the other two terms).
The first line of the boxed formula has a prime on zeta: zeta'^*_{E_y}(1/(qt)), presumably meaning the dual representation.
'-i_*(E'_y) - i_*(E_y)' should be read as the start of the exact sequence 0 -> i_*(E'_y) -> i_*(E_y) -> ...
The sum runs over x a 'pt de non-simplicité de E''_y'; the boxed side note reads '[ensemble] fini des pts de "non-simplicité" de E''_y'.
In the first line of the 'D'où' system the middle term is L^*_{E'_y} L^*_{E''_y} L_Q(t)^{-1}. In the second line the second factor reads L^*_{E''_y} (double prime in the image).
